editorial:
Imagine waking up every day dreading school because the most popular girl in class has decided to make your life a living hell. That is exactly what happens to Jessica, a sweet girl who just wants to get through her sophomore year. Avery is the kind of mean girl you love to hate, and she spends her time mocking Jessica and turning everyone against her. The whole movie feels like a warning sign, building up a lot of tension as you watch Jessica struggle with the constant bullying and the feeling of being totally alone. It is a heavy story, but it captures that scary high school feeling perfectly.

What really makes this work is how it uses a documentary style to show the aftermath of a huge event. The acting feels real, and the twist in the middle of the film completely changes how you see the story. While some parts feel a bit like a TV movie, the message about bullying is powerful. You should definitely watch this if you like emotional dramas that teach a lesson.
endingExplained: The story takes a dark turn when it is revealed that Jessica actually took her own life because of the bullying. The documentary crew shows footage from a hidden camera that proves how cruel Avery was. Avery is forced to face the guilt and the legal consequences of her actions. The movie ends with a strong message to the community, showing that words have real power and that bullying can have permanent, tragic results.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful stories about high school and social issues.
